question.problem: Given the function $f(x,y)=\operatorname{sin}⁡({x}^{2}-y)$ find the equation of the tangent line to the level curve that passes through the point where $(x,y)=(0,\pi ).$
question.worked_solution:
The equation of the tangent line to the level curve $f(x,y)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

First, we find the gradient of $f(x,y)$ and evaluate it at $(x,y)=(0,\pi ):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & ={f}_{x}(x,y)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y)\,j \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡({x}^{2}-y))\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{sin}⁡({x}^{2}-y))\,j \\  & =2x\operatorname{cos}⁡({x}^{2}-y)\,i-\operatorname{cos}⁡({x}^{2}-y)\,j \\ ∇f(0,\pi ) & =2(0)\operatorname{cos}⁡({0}^{2}-\pi )\,i-\operatorname{cos}⁡({0}^{2}-\pi )\,j \\  & =0\,i+j \\  & =⟨0,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the Cartesian equation of the tangent line to the level curve that passes through the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0})$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(0,\pi )\cdot ⟨x-0,\,y-\pi ⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨0,1⟩\cdot ⟨x,\,y-\pi ⟩ & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
